result.topic_en: Euler sets up Problem II, finding the regular (pendulum-like) vibration modes of an elastic rod, by reducing the motion to the equation $y = f^4\,d^4y/ds^4$ and trying an exponential solution $y = e^{\lambda s}$.
result.transcription:
) 112 (

Problema II.

§. 9. Cum virga noſtra infinitis modis contremiſcere queat, eos caſus in genere inueſtigare, quibus ejus motus vibratorius euadet regularis, ſeu minimis oſcillationibus penduli cuiuſpiam ſimplicis conformis.

Solutio.

Ponamus igitur longitudinem iſtius penduli ſimplicis $= k$, atque vt motus virgae pari modo peragatur, neceſſe eſt vt ſit $\frac{1}{2g}\left(\frac{ddy}{dt^2}\right) = -\frac{y}{k}$; in qua aequatione cum ſolum tempus $t$ pro variabili habeatur, longitudo vero $s$ vt conſtans ſpectetur, per duplicem integrationem peruenitur ad iſtam formulam generalem:
$y = M\,\text{ſin.}\left(\zeta + t\sqrt{\frac{2g}{k}}\right)$,
vbi quantitas, M non ſolum eſt conſtans, ſed etiam functionem quamcunque ipſius $s$ deſignare poteſt. Cum igitur per aequationem finalem ſit
$\frac{1}{2g}\left(\frac{ddy}{dt^2}\right) = -bcc\left(\frac{d^4y}{ds^4}\right)$,
erit etiam $bcc\left(\frac{d^4y}{ds^4}\right) = \frac{y}{k}$; in qua aequatione ſola quantitas $s$ pro variabili aſſumitur, cuius ergo integrale inueſtigari oportet. Quod quo facilius fieri poſſit ponamus breuitatis gratia $bcck = f^4$, vt remotis clauſulis iam ſit $y = \frac{f^4\,d^4y}{ds^4}$, cui ſatisfieri poſſe euidens eſt huiusmodi valore: $y = e^{\lambda s}$. Quia enim hinc fit
$\frac{dy}{ds} = \lambda e^{\lambda s}$, $\frac{ddy}{ds^2} = \lambda\lambda e^{\lambda s}$, $\frac{d^3y}{ds^3} = \lambda^3 e^{\lambda s}$, $\frac{d^4y}{ds^4} = \lambda^4 e^{\lambda s}$,
his ſubſtitutis prodit iſta aequalitas: $1 = \lambda^4 f^4$, ſiue

items.english: Since our rod can vibrate in infinitely many ways, to investigate in general those cases in which its vibratory motion becomes regular, that is, conforming to the very small oscillations of some simple pendulum.

items.quote: cui ſatisfieri poſſe euidens eſt huiusmodi valore: $y = e^{\lambda s}$
items.english: It is evident that this equation can be satisfied by a value of the form $y = e^{\lambda s}$.
